intro: Finding the perfect swimming hairstyles can be the difference between gorgeous summer waves and a tangled, chlorine-damaged nightmare. Whether you are lounging by a resort pool or doing daily laps, protecting your strands from harsh chemicals is a must. Chlorine strips your hair of its natural oils, leaving it brittle, dry, and prone to breakage. The secret to keeping your hair healthy all summer is a combination of protective styling and the right hair accessories. From chic silk scrunchies that will not snag wet hair to leave-in conditioners you can wear under a stylish swim cap, these protective looks and essential products will keep your mane looking flawless. Let us dive into the best ways to protect your hair while still looking cute poolside!

picks.description: A high top knot is one of the most classic swimming hairstyles because it keeps the majority of your ends completely out of the water. However, securing wet heavy hair with a standard elastic can cause severe breakage. Swapping your regular hair tie for an oversized mulberry silk scrunchie is a game-changer for pool days. Silk glides effortlessly over wet strands, preventing the friction and snapping that leads to frizz. Simply gather your hair at the very top of your head, twist it gently into a loose bun, and wrap the silk scrunchie around it twice. This look is effortlessly chic for lounging poolside with a cocktail in hand, and it guarantees you will not be ripping out clumps of hair when it is time to take your updo down at the end of the day.
picks.best_for: Keeping long hair completely dry while lounging poolside.
picks.quirky_fact: Silk absorbs significantly less moisture than cotton, meaning your scrunchie will not become a heavy, soggy mess if it accidentally gets splashed.

picks.description: If you plan on actually swimming underwater, a slicked-back braided ponytail paired with a pre-swim hair defense cream is your best line of defense. Hair is like a sponge; if you fill it with clean water and a protective barrier cream before jumping in, it cannot absorb as much chlorinated pool water. Generously coat your damp hair with a specialized pre-swim cream, brush it straight back, and secure it into a tight braid. The cream acts as a physical shield against harsh chemicals, copper, and salt, while the tight braid prevents your hair from tangling into a massive knot while you swim. This powerful combination ensures that when you finally wash your hair post-swim, it feels incredibly soft and hydrated rather than feeling like a pile of dry straw.
picks.best_for: Active swimmers who want to submerge their head completely.
picks.quirky_fact: Wetting your hair with fresh tap water before applying the cream helps lock the barrier in place much more effectively.
picks.shop_query: pre swim hair defense cream chlorine protection

picks.description: Sometimes the best swimming hairstyles are the ones that take absolutely zero effort. A twisted crown updo held securely by a jumbo matte claw clip is stylish, incredibly fast, and keeps your ends far away from the chlorine. When shopping for pool accessories, opt for a matte rubberized claw clip rather than a shiny plastic one. The rubberized texture provides a superior grip on slippery, wet hair, ensuring your updo stays perfectly in place even if you are splashing around in the shallow end. To achieve the look, gather your hair at the nape of your neck, twist it tightly upward, and clamp the clip securely over the twist. Let the ends cascade over the top for a relaxed, effortless summer aesthetic that looks beautiful in vacation photos.
picks.best_for: Quick, effortless styling for thick or curly hair types.
picks.quirky_fact: The flat-lay design of some modern claw clips allows you to comfortably lean back on a pool lounger without the clip digging into your scalp.
picks.shop_query: jumbo matte rubberized claw clip non slip

picks.description: A sleek low chignon is a beautiful, sophisticated look for the beach club, but the sun beating down on your exposed scalp and strands can cause severe color fading. Pairing your elegant low bun with a high-quality UV protection hair mist ensures your expensive salon color stays vibrant all summer long. Formulated with UV filters and hydrating botanical extracts, this lightweight spray acts just like sunscreen for your hair. Part your hair neatly down the middle, spray the mist generously from root to tip, and twist your hair into a smooth bun at the nape of your neck. The mist will give your hair a glossy, polished finish while actively blocking out the suns harmful rays and preventing the pool water from oxidizing your gorgeous highlights.
picks.best_for: Color-treated hair that is prone to fading in the summer sun.
picks.quirky_fact: UV hair mists often contain sunflower seed extract, which is naturally rich in antioxidants and provides incredible natural protection against color degradation.
picks.shop_query: UV protection hair mist color treated hair

picks.description: A classic French braid is a staple among swimming hairstyles because it securely locks every single layer of your hair in place, preventing the dreaded underwater tangles. However, finishing the braid with a traditional metal-clasped elastic is a recipe for disaster on wet hair. Seamless silicone hair ties are an absolute necessity for this look. Unlike fabric or metal-bound ties, silicone grips wet hair perfectly without absorbing any chlorinated water. They will not stretch out, snap, or pull your hair when you remove them. Weaving your hair into a tight French braid keeps the cuticle smooth and protected, drastically reducing the amount of friction your hair experiences while swimming laps. Just remember to braid firmly but not so tight that it pulls uncomfortably at your delicate hairline.
picks.best_for: Layered hair that tends to escape from traditional ponytails and buns.
picks.quirky_fact: You can shrink stretched-out silicone hair ties back to their original size by simply dropping them into a mug of hot water for a few minutes.
picks.shop_query: seamless silicone hair ties snag free

picks.description: Double Dutch braids are incredibly trendy, practical, and perfect for a full day of water activities. To make this style truly protective against chlorine, you need to prep your strands with a rich, nourishing protective Argan hair oil. The oil creates a hydrophobic barrier, meaning it literally repels the pool water away from your hair shaft. Before braiding, distribute a generous few pumps of Argan oil evenly through your dry or damp hair, focusing heavily on the fragile ends. Divide your hair down the center and create two tight Dutch braids. The oil will not only protect your hair from chemical damage but will also act as an intensive deep conditioning treatment while you bake in the sun. When you undo the braids, you will be left with gorgeous, frizz-free mermaid waves.
picks.best_for: Creating a deep-conditioning heat treatment while you enjoy the sun.
picks.quirky_fact: Argan oil is naturally packed with Vitamin E, which helps increase hair elasticity and prevents strands from snapping when wet.
picks.shop_query: 100 percent pure organic argan oil hair

picks.description: If you are serious about keeping your hair completely dry and protected from chlorine, nothing beats a physical barrier. Forget the tight, uncomfortable latex caps of your high school swim team days; modern vintage-style textured swim caps are incredibly chic and highly functional. These caps often feature beautiful three-dimensional floral details or elegant ruching that looks straight out of a classic Hollywood movie. Underneath the stylish exterior, they provide a waterproof seal that keeps your blowout completely intact. To wear it properly, twist your hair into a flat pin curl against your head and stretch the cap gently over your ears. It is the ultimate statement accessory for a luxury resort pool, ensuring you can swim your heart out without ever having to worry about washing and restyling your hair afterward.
picks.best_for: Complete water protection and maintaining a fresh blowout.
picks.quirky_fact: Many retro swim caps feature a softer, fabric-lined interior that prevents the rubber from painfully pulling on your baby hairs around the edges.
picks.shop_query: vintage style textured floral swim cap

picks.description: A scarf-wrapped bun offers a beautiful, bohemian vibe while providing excellent protection for your hair at the pool. Upgrading to a specialized waterproof hair scarf takes this look to the next level. These innovative scarves are designed with water-resistant materials that look and feel like luxurious silk but repel splashes and pool water effortlessly. Gather your hair into a high bun, secure it with a soft scrunchie, and fold the waterproof scarf into a long triangle. Wrap it around the base of your bun or tie it over your crown like a stylish headband. This style expertly hides any messy pool hair while protecting your scalp from sunburn and your ends from chlorine. It is the perfect accessory to transition your look seamlessly from a daytime pool party to an evening dinner.
picks.best_for: Adding a pop of color to your swimsuit while protecting your scalp.
picks.quirky_fact: Wrapping a scarf around your bun adds extra volume, making your hair look incredibly thick and glamorous even when it is pinned up.

picks.description: The slicked-back wet look is highly fashionable and ridiculously easy to achieve, making it one of the absolute best swimming hairstyles for short to medium hair. The trick to nailing this aesthetic while protecting your hair is using a heavy-duty chlorine-blocking leave-in conditioner. Instead of using a standard hair gel that will flake and wash away in the pool, heavily saturate your hair with the leave-in conditioner and comb it straight back with a wide-tooth comb. The conditioner gives you that sleek, high-fashion wet look while infusing your strands with vital proteins and moisture. The thick barrier prevents chlorine from penetrating the hair shaft, and the slicked-back style ensures your hair stays out of your face while you swim. It is modern, edgy, and incredibly beneficial for your hair health.
picks.best_for: Short bobs or medium-length hair that cannot easily fit into a bun or braid.
picks.quirky_fact: Chlorine-blocking conditioners often contain Vitamin C, which actively neutralizes chlorine and prevents blonde hair from turning that dreaded shade of green.
picks.shop_query: chlorine blocking leave in conditioner swim

picks.description: Managing baby hairs and bangs at the pool can be incredibly frustrating, especially when they dry into frizzy, unmanageable curls after touching chlorine. A sleek neoprene swim headband is the ultimate solution for keeping your edges protected and perfectly laid. Neoprene is the exact same material used in wetsuits, meaning it is highly durable, water-resistant, and provides a snug, comfortable fit without giving you a headache. Pull your hair back into your favorite swimming hairstyle, and slide the neoprene headband over your hairline, ensuring it covers your ears to keep water out. It is a fantastic, sporty look that keeps flyaways locked down, prevents water from dripping into your eyes, and protects your delicate baby hairs from the harsh, drying effects of pool chemicals.
picks.best_for: Taming bangs, protecting baby hairs, and keeping water out of your ears.
picks.quirky_fact: Neoprene is an excellent insulator, which means these headbands also help regulate your body temperature if you are swimming in a slightly chilly pool.

faqs.question: Should I wet my hair before getting into the pool?
faqs.answer: Yes, absolutely! Your hair is like a sponge. If you thoroughly soak it with clean tap water before jumping into the pool, it will absorb significantly less of the chlorinated water. For even better protection, apply a leave-in conditioner or a specialized pre-swim cream right after wetting it.

faqs.question: How can I prevent my blonde hair from turning green in chlorine?
faqs.answer: The green tint is actually caused by oxidized copper in the pool water binding to the proteins in your hair. To prevent this, always wet your hair with fresh water first, use a protective barrier cream, and wash your hair immediately after swimming with a clarifying or Vitamin C-based shampoo.

faqs.question: Are braids or buns better for swimming?
faqs.answer: Both are excellent, but they serve different purposes. A high bun is best if you want to keep your hair completely out of the water while lounging. If you plan on actually swimming underwater, tight braids are superior because they prevent your hair from tangling and matting while fully submerged.

faqs.question: Is it safe to leave pool water in my hair to dry?
faqs.answer: No, you should never let chlorinated water dry in your hair. As the water evaporates, it leaves behind concentrated pool chemicals that strip your hair of its natural oils, leading to severe dryness and breakage. Always rinse your hair thoroughly with fresh water immediately after exiting the pool.
